headline: Deforestation of the Amazon rainforest
details: Brazilian environment minister João Paulo Capobianco reports that deforestation in Brazil's Amazon rainforest fell to 5796 km² in the year through July 2026, the lowest level since 1988 except for 2012. (AFP via France 24)

headline: Australia–Fiji relations
details: Australia agrees to provide Fiji with solar-, wind-, and wave-powered Bluebottle maritime drones and training for surveillance and efforts against drug trafficking and other transnational crime, with deployment expected in 2027. (AFP via RFI)

headline: Hungary–Ukraine relations, Accession of Ukraine to the European Union
details: Hungarian prime minister Péter Magyar and Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy agree to improve bilateral relations during a meeting in Brussels, Belgium, with Hungary lifting objections to further European Union accession talks for Ukraine following progress on ethnic Hungarian minority rights in Ukraine. (Reuters)

headline: 2026 anti-CEC protests
details: Cockroach Janta Party leader Abhijeet Dipke is detained in Delhi, India, ahead of the party's planned march. (BBC News)

headline: South African police rescue about 200 people from an unregistered rehabilitation centre in Mpumalanga and arrest two people while investigating alleged kidnapping and health and safety violations.
details: Fourteen people receive medical treatment following the rescue. (Reuters)

headline: 2026 WXV Global Series
details: In women's rugby union, Canada defeats England 24–21 in a WXV Global Series match in Toronto, ending the Red Roses' four-year unbeaten run at 41 matches (the longest in rugby union history) after Shoshanah Seumanutafa scores a late try. (Stuff)

headline: Yemeni civil war
details: Houthi–Saudi conflict
Saudi Arabia says that it has intercepted a missile intended for Medina. However, the Houthis denied launching a missile at the city. (The Hill) (France 24)

The Houthis launch missiles against Al-Maashiq Palace, headquarters of the Presidential Leadership Council and official residence of President Rashad al-Alimi, in Aden, Yemen, killing five people and injuring 16. No member of the council is harmed in the attack. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)

headline: Capital punishment in the United States
details: U.S. president Donald Trump announces that the Department of Defense has reversed its plan to livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, scheduled for December 3. (AFP via France 24) (AP)

headline: Argentine police arrest at least 25 people after clashes during a university funding protest in Buenos Aires, while eight police officers are injured. (AFP via France 24)
details: Argentine police arrest at least 25 people after clashes during a university funding protest in Buenos Aires, while eight police officers are injured. (AFP via France 24)

headline: Northern Irish politician and former Democratic Unionist Party leader Jeffrey Donaldson is sentenced to 15 years in prison for child sexual abuse and rape.
details: The offences occurred between 1985 and 2008. (AP) (BBC News)

headline: Astronomers discover the first green star, WD J1330+6435, according to a study published by RAS Techniques and Instruments. (Popular Science)
details: Astronomers discover the first green star, WD J1330+6435, according to a study published by RAS Techniques and Instruments. (Popular Science)

headline: At the General Conference on Weights and Measures, the International Bureau of Weights and Measures votes to abolish future leap seconds and make Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) continuous, starting 20 May 2027.
details: To account for future differences between UTC and International Atomic Time, a leap hour will be observed as needed. (The Guardian) (Scientific American)

headline: 2026 Major League Baseball season
details: In baseball, the Milwaukee Brewers sweep the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS to advance to the 2026 World Series, their first since 1982. (ESPN)

headline: China–North Korea relations
details: The New Yalu River Bridge connecting Dandong, China, and Sinuiju, North Korea, opens following a 12-year delay. (BBC News) (NK News)

headline: The European Central Bank authorizes UniCredit to raise its stake in Commerzbank above 30% without an upper limit, allowing the Italian bank to proceed toward taking control of the German lender. (The Eastern Herald)
details: The European Central Bank authorizes UniCredit to raise its stake in Commerzbank above 30% without an upper limit, allowing the Italian bank to proceed toward taking control of the German lender. (The Eastern Herald)

headline: 2026 Peshawar school roof collapse
details: A roof collapses at a school in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killing 34 students and a teacher, and injuring 50 more people. (BBC News)

headline: 2026 Indonesia wildfires
details: Four people are killed fighting wildfires in Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java, Indonesia, after flames and thick smoke trapped them. Two others suffer serious burns. (AFP)

headline: Seven people are missing after a San Marino-flagged tanker catches fire off the coast of Romania amid recent drone attacks on merchant shipping in the Black Sea.
details: Search and rescue operations are underway to locate the missing crew members. (Politico)

headline: The United Kingdom declares a severe drought in Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex, and West Sussex after prolonged low rainfall left more than 80% of England in drought and major reservoirs below 20% capacity. (AFP)
details: The United Kingdom declares a severe drought in Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex, and West Sussex after prolonged low rainfall left more than 80% of England in drought and major reservoirs below 20% capacity. (AFP)

headline: Germany–Iran relations, Antisemitism in 21st-century Germany, Iranian external operations
details: A court in Hamburg, Germany, sentences a Danish national to eight years and six months in prison and an Afghan national to four years and six months in prison for plotting to assassinate Josef Schuster, the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, on behalf of Iran. (Reuters)

headline: 2026 Silver Rail Elementary School shooting
details: Three children and a teacher are killed in a mass school shooting at the Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, United States. Two other people are wounded. The perpetrator, a 16-year-old male, is shot and killed by a bystander. (AP) (The Guardian)

headline: Middle Eastern crisis
details: Yemeni civil war
Houthi–Saudi conflict
The Houthis claim to have shot down a Royal Saudi Air Force Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft over Saada Governorate, Yemen. Saudi authorities did not comment on the claim. (AFP via AA)
The Saudi Civil Defense reports that debris from intercepted Houthi cruise missiles injured four people, including a child, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and damaged 15 homes. (AFP via CNA)
2026 Iran war
2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis

Two cargo ships, the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride and the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged dry bulk carrier Cape Dao, sink after both are attacked by projectiles near the Strait of Hormuz while trying to navigate through what Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps called an "illegal and dangerous route." At least one crew member is killed in the attacks. (The Guardian) (Reuters)

headline: Censorship in Turkey
details: Turkish opposition-leaning and independent news channel Halk TV goes offline as it is raided by police and new administrators are appointed by the government. (BBC News)

headline: Internet censorship in Mexico
details: President Claudia Sheinbaum signs a decree banning violent content on social media to protect minors under the age of 18. (Expansión)

headline: Costa Rica inaugurates, a maximum-security prison modeled after El Salvador's CECOT mega-prison, aimed at holding 20% of the country's current prison population, as the homicide rate reached a record high in 2023. (Reuters)
details: Costa Rica inaugurates, a maximum-security prison modeled after El Salvador's CECOT mega-prison, aimed at holding 20% of the country's current prison population, as the homicide rate reached a record high in 2023. (Reuters)

headline: 2026 Irish public sector strikes
details: Over 300,000 public sector workers in Ireland, including teachers, health workers, and other civil servants, start a general strike, the first in the country since 2009, to protest against a deadlock in pay negotiations. (Reuters)

headline: Kekova shipwreck
details: The oldest known shipwreck in the world (2700–2400 BC) is excavated in Kekova, Turkey. (CNN)

headline: Russo-Ukrainian war
details: Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
A Russian ballistic missile attack strikes a power station in the Dniprovskyi District, Kyiv, Ukraine, leaving more than 1,000 residential buildings without heating. (BBC News)

headline: Sudanese civil war
details: Darfur campaign

The Sudanese Armed Forces announces that they have re-captured the Bir Kelekel area of West Darfur, Sudan, from Rapid Support Forces, according to West Darfur state governor Bahr al-Din Adam Karama. (Radio Tamazuj) (AA)

headline: Flamingo Revolution
details: Rioters attack government buildings, banks, businesses and other sites as anti-government protests erupt in Tirana, Albania. At least 23 police officers and six others are injured during the unrest, while 35 people are detained. President Bajram Begaj condemns the violence and appeals for calm across the nation. (AP)

headline: Three people are killed and four others are missing after torrential rainfall triggers widespread flooding across Istanbul, Turkey. (ABC News)
details: Three people are killed and four others are missing after torrential rainfall triggers widespread flooding across Istanbul, Turkey. (ABC News)

headline: 2026 Southeast Asian haze
details: Singapore records its highest air pollution level of 2026 as one-hour PM concentrations reach about 288 micrograms per cubic metre amid haze from Indonesian wildfires. (AFP)
Timor-Leste suspends in-person classes nationwide from October 15 to 17 due to worsening air quality from wildfire smoke and pollutant particles across Southeast Asia. (AFP)

headline: Colombia–Israel relations
details: Colombia opens an embassy in Jerusalem and restores its free trade agreement with Israel. (Reuters)

headline: Russo-Ukrainian war
details: Nord Stream pipelines sabotage
The Ukrainian citizen accused of sabotaging the Nord Stream pipelines in 2022 faces trial at the Higher Regional Court in Hamburg, Germany, (DW) (UPI)

headline: 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
details: A court in New Delhi, India, remands Cockroach Janta Party spokespeople Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka in custody for five days after police detained them for entering the restricted Jantar Mantar protest site. (AFP via RFI)

headline: Middle Eastern crisis
details: Yemeni civil war
Houthi–Saudi conflict
The Royal Saudi Air Force strikes a fuel depot near Sanaa, Yemen. The Houthis launch missiles upon multiple Saudi Arabian cities, including Riyadh and Dammam, in response. (BBC News) (CNN)

An administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Dhahran, Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia, is partially consumed by a fire after a Houthi missile is intercepted over the city by Saudi forces. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
Hezbollah–Israel conflict, Funding of Hezbollah

Hezbollah spokesperson Ali Damoush announces that the group will pay up to US$14,000 in aid to families whose homes in Lebanon were destroyed or rendered uninhabitable during its war with Israel. Families in Beirut and its suburbs will receive $14,000, while those elsewhere in the country will receive $12,000. (AP)

headline: Murder of Tupac Shakur
details: The Clark County District Court in Nevada, United States, sentences former Crips gang leader Duane "Keffe D" Davis to a minimum of 40 years in prison for orchestrating the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur in Las Vegas. (AFP via France 24) (DW)

headline: North Korean remote worker scheme
details: The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation announces the arrests of two men in Ohio and Pennsylvania over an alleged North Korean remote-work scheme and the seizures of about 187 computers and related devices from more than 40 suspected laptop farms in Texas. (AFP via Malay Mail)

headline: Scam centers in Myanmar
details: A Chinese court sentences three triad members to death for crimes linked to scam centers in Kokang, Myanmar, including fraud, drug trafficking, illegal gambling, prostitution, and the murders of two Chinese citizens. (AFP via CBS News)

headline: Four people are killed and three more injured in a mass shooting at a memorial service in Katlehong, Gauteng, South Africa. (AP)
details: Four people are killed and three more injured in a mass shooting at a memorial service in Katlehong, Gauteng, South Africa. (AP)

headline: Three Indian nationals are killed and five others are injured in a suspected arson attack in Bochum, North Rhine-Westphalia Germany.
details: A 41-year-old resident is arrested. (tagesschau)

headline: Eight people are injured in a mass stabbing at a supermarket in Incheon, South Korea.
details: A suspect is arrested. (BBC News) (CNA)

headline: Students in Tirana, Albania, throw bricks at the Ministry of Education building, prompting riot police to respond. (Reuters)
details: Students in Tirana, Albania, throw bricks at the Ministry of Education building, prompting riot police to respond. (Reuters)

headline: 2026 World Artistic Gymnastics Championships
details: The Netherlands denies visas to Russian artistic gymnasts Anna Kalmykova, Viktoria Listunova, and Angelina Melnikova for the world championships in Rotterdam, while four other Russian gymnasts receive permission to enter the country. (AP)

headline: In auto racing, Formula 1 announces a new grand prix in Kigali, Rwanda, to run for at least 10 years starting in the early 2030s with a new track.
details: This would be the first F1 grand prix in Africa since South Africa in 1993. (AP)

headline: Russo-Ukrainian war
details: Bulgaria–Russia relations, Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war

Two merchant ships are hit by unknown drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, with one sinking. Eleven crew members are missing and 20 in total are rescued. Bulgarian prime minister Rumen Radev has blamed Russia and summoned its ambassador. It is the second such attack in six days. (Reuters)

headline: 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
details: Six deaths are confirmed in Florida, United States, from Hurricane Isaias. (Fox Weather) (The Guardian)

headline: 2026 Multan train derailment
details: At least seven people are killed and over 40 others are injured in a train derailment near Multan, Punjab, Pakistan. (AA) (AFP via The Straits Times)

headline: Famine in Yemen, Water supply and sanitation in Yemen
details: The World Health Organization reports a surge in cholera cases in Yemen over the past three weeks. The country previously had a 6-year-long outbreak due to the ongoing humanitarian crisis. (AFP via Arab News)

headline: Indonesian authorities release 20 protected green sea turtles back into the oceans off Bali after they were seized from an empty boat abandoned by wildlife smugglers last week. (AP)
details: Indonesian authorities release 20 protected green sea turtles back into the oceans off Bali after they were seized from an empty boat abandoned by wildlife smugglers last week. (AP)

headline: 2024 Cornell University rape allegations
details: Cornell University in Ithaca, New York, United States, suspends all fraternity parties and social events for the remainder of the 2026–27 academic year following allegations that seven Chi Phi members drugged and gang-raped a student in 2024. (AFP) (BBC News)

headline: Impeachment trial of Sara Duterte
details: Philippine prosecutors in the impeachment trial of vice president Sara Duterte drop three of the four impeachment charges in an attempt to speed up the trial. The Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, approves the move. (AP)

headline: LGBTQ rights in Hungary
details: The Hungarian National Assembly passes an amendment repealing most provisions of the anti-LGBTQ child protection law that was previously passed during former prime minister Viktor Orbán's tenure in 2021. (DW)

details: Houthi–Saudi conflict
October 2026 attacks on Saudi Arabia airports
The Houthis claim to have attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with a ballistic missile for a third consecutive day. (Reuters)
Delta Air Lines postpones direct flights from Atlanta's Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport to Riyadh following attacks by the Houthis on the country. (The Hill)

headline: 2026 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa state of emergency
details: Pakistan's federal government detains hundreds of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) members, including former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi and other provincial officials, after suspending the PTI-led provincial administration and imposing emergency rule. (AFP via RFI)

headline: 2026 French supermarket cyber attack

headline: 2026 Great Wolf Lodge stabbings
details: A woman stabs her husband and her 3-year-old son to death while on vacation at a Great Wolf Lodge in Pennsylvania. (ABC News)

headline: 2026 Estonian presidential election
details: Ülle Madise, who was elected by the Riigikogu in September, takes office as President of Estonia, succeeding Alar Karis. (Estonian World)

headline: Generative AI chatbot company Character.ai files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, citing costs and litigations including those linked to teen suicides. (The Wall Street Journal) (CBS News)
details: Generative AI chatbot company Character.ai files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, citing costs and litigations including those linked to teen suicides. (The Wall Street Journal) (CBS News)

details: M23 campaign

Former Congolese president Joseph Kabila announces the formation of a rebel political-military coalition named Front for the Refoundation of the Nation, which includes the March 23 Movement, Twirwaneho and the Congo River Alliance. The group, led by Kabila, says it aimed to coordinate "resistance forces" to topple the Government of President Félix Tshisekedi. (BBC)

headline: 2026 Nobel Prizes
details: American economists Robert Ernest Hall and Michael Dean Woodford are jointly awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for their work on "microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation". (CNN)

headline: American visual images company Getty Images announces that it will file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. (Reuters)
details: American visual images company Getty Images announces that it will file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. (Reuters)

details: Two deaths are reported after hurricanes Rachel and Simon made landfall on Mexico's coast, with Guerrero governor Evelyn Salgado and Baja California governor Marina del Pilar Ávila confirming their deaths. (Al Jazeera)

details: One person is killed and four others are injured after an accident on the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia in Mableton, Georgia, United States. (BNO News)

headline: A fire destroys the historic Marché des Enfants-Rouges food market in Paris, France. (France 24)
details: A fire destroys the historic Marché des Enfants-Rouges food market in Paris, France. (France 24)

headline: International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Russia–European Union relations
details: The Council of the European Union approves the 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, targeting 1,569 individuals and entities of the country's military and industrial complex. (EU Council)

headline: 2026 Aubagne school shooting
details: A 14-year-old student opens fire at a middle school in Aubagne, France, injuring two staff members, before being detained. (AP) (France 24)

Houthi–Saudi conflict
October 2026 attacks on Saudi Arabia airports

Houthis launch an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, causing a fire, killing one person and injuring multiple people. (Sky News) (Al Jazeera)
An Indian national injured in yesterday's attack on King Khalid International Airport dies from his injuries, raising the total death toll to 13. (Reuters)
The Royal Saudi Air Force launches an airstrike in Sanaa, Yemen, killing a child and wounding seven other people. (Al Jazeera)
2026 Iran war

details: The Indonesian forestry ministry and International Animal Rescue release eight orangutans rescued from wildfires into a protected wildforest in West Kalimantan after fires destroyed habitat near plantations. (AFP)

details: An executive magistrate's court in New Delhi, India, orders the release of Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders, requiring them to avoid breaches of the peace for one year after their detention. (AFP via France 24)

details: Independent candidate Łukasz Gibała wins the Kraków mayoral election in Poland against government-backed Civic Platform senator Monika Piątkowska. (Politico) (Euronews)

details: Pakistani president Asif Ali Zardari declares a state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and suspends its provincial government amid disputes over the province's response to Islamist militancy. (AFP via RFI)

headline: 2027 French presidential election
details: Raphaël Glucksmann is elected as a candidate in the 2027 French presidential election during the Socialist Party primary, receiving more than 66% of the votes in the first round. (AFP via RFI)

Airstrikes are launched at the Egypt–Sudan border targeting an artisanal gold mine in a mountainous area, killing at least 72 people. (Sky News)

details: Three civilians and two police officers are killed in a mass shooting in Jacona, Michoacán, Mexico, while six other people are wounded. Separately, three gunmen are killed in a shootout with police in Zamora. (OEM in Spanish)

details: Four FARC dissidents are killed and 12 rifles seized after an airstrike by the National Army of Colombia against a guerrilla camp in Norte de Santander Department, Colombia. (El Tiempo in Spanish)
A drone strike kills a soldier in La Vega, Cauca Department, Colombia. (Publimetro in Spanish)

headline: 2026 Budhi Gandaki flood
details: Ten people are reported missing and at least 35 houses and six bridges are swept away in a major flash flood in Gorkha District, Gandaki Province, Nepal. The exact number of casualties is unknown. (ANI via Gulf News) (Nepal Views)

details: At least 139 people are killed, 84 more are missing, and over 80 are rescued when a boat carrying migrants shipwrecks off the coast of Djibouti. (AFP via France 24)

details: The Kenyan health ministry reports that no Ebola cases have been reported since one patient died from the disease on October 5, with 293 tests conducted. (Reuters)

2026 Eritrean incursion into Ethiopia

Ethiopian forces regain control of Adigrat in the Tigray Region following a withdrawal of Eritrean forces. Celebrations are reported in the city following the withdrawal. (Oman Observer) (Al Jazeera) (UA News)

headline: 2026 NCAA Division I FBS football season
details: In American college football, the Kentucky Wildcats football team defeats the LSU Tigers 35–34 on a 2-point conversion in overtime, becoming the first team in FBS history to win consecutive overtime games by one point since overtime was introduced in 1996. (The Athletic via The New York Times) (The Score)

headline: 2026 Il Lombardia
details: In cycling, French cyclist Paul Seixas wins the 120th edition of the Giro di Lombardia in Italy, becoming the youngest person to do so. (NBC Sports) (The Guardian)

At least 20 people are killed and 32 others are injured in a Russian glide bomb airstrike on a five-story residential building in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine. (Ukrainska Pravda)

headline: 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
details: The National Hurricane Center reports that Hurricane Isaias has weakened to a post-tropical cyclone after making landfall near Destin, Florida, United States. (WVTM-TV) (NBC News)
Four people are killed during Isaias' landfall in the United States, with two deaths in Escambia County, Florida, and another two in Alabama. (The Guardian)

headline: 2026 Pacific hurricane season
details: Tropical storm Simon strengthens into a category 4 Pacific hurricane with 150 mph (240 kph) winds as it heads towards Mexico's coast. (AP) (The Rio Times)

details: The tiger was uninjured. (BBC News)

Indian authorities are placing New Delhi under a security lockdown and have been detaining thousands of demonstrators to block a rally organized by the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party. (BBC News) (The Guardian) (The New York Times)

headline: 2026 Poland school stabbings
details: A woman carries out a mass stabbing at an adult school in Warsaw, Poland, injuring three people. The suspect is arrested. It is the third such attack in the country in a week. (AP)

details: In association football, the match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Bilbao is abandoned by referee José María Sánchez Martínez due to fans throwing objects at the pitch to protest against Rayo president Raúl Martín Presa. (Reuters)

The Pentagon raises the U.S. military death toll in the Iran war to 21 after reporting two noncombat deaths. (The Hill)

details: Six people suspected of stealing Pierre-Auguste Renoir's paintings Young Woman at the Well and Madame Colonna Romano from the Musée Renoir in Cagnes-sur-Mer, Alpes-Maritimes, France, are arrested, and the artworks are recovered. (AP) (Reuters)

headline: 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
details: South African judge and former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Navi Pillay is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for "her efforts to promote peace and international law". (DW)

headline: Shootings by U.S. immigration agents in the second Trump administration
details: Clashes erupt in New York City, United States, between protestors and police after the shooting of a Dominican Republic national with a criminal conviction by ICE agents. The man, who was in a car alongside a child, was then detained while being wounded. (Al Jazeera)

headline: 2026 Erie shooting
details: Eight people are killed, including the perpetrator, in a mass shooting at a home in Erie, Pennsylvania, United States. (AP) (BBC News)

details: The hostages are rescued, with two children sustaining injuries. (AP)

headline: Next Palestinian legislative election
details: Palestinian vice president Hussein al-Sheikh announces that the Palestinian legislative election planned for November 28 will be postponed, possibly until September 2027, along with the also delayed presidential election, because of worsening conditions throughout Palestine. (Reuters)

details: Czechs begin voting in the first round to elect one-third of the Senate. Incumbent prime minister Andrej Babiš seeks gains of his coalition in the Senate. Municipal elections are also underway. (AP)

details: However, President Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani reappoints Diay, asking him to form a new government. (AFP via Arab News)
